# Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination

**RE: Appeal of Denial — Total Hip Replacement (CPT 27130)**
**Member:** Rowan Brooks
**Member ID:** W772624569
**Reference Number:** POC-A5F6D22435-38075
**Date of Denial Notice:** 2026-08-07
**Plan:** Security Health Plan (Commercial/ACA), Wisconsin

**Governing Policy Cited in This Review:** eviCore CMM-311/312/313/314/315/601/606/609 series (generic EviCore editions) — *Comprehensive Musculoskeletal Management Guidelines V2.0.2025*
https://www.evicore.com/sites/default/files/clinical-guidelines/2025-08/EviCore_CMM-311%20Knee%20Replacement%20Arthroplasty_V2.0.2025_Eff11.05.2025_upd08.12.2025.pdf

---

Dear Security Health Plan Appeals Department,

I am appealing the denial of my prior authorization request for a total hip replacement (CPT 27130), denied on 2026-08-07 under reference number POC-A5F6D22435-38075. I am asking the plan to reconsider this decision. My surgeon, Dr. Lindqvist, has documented that this procedure is medically necessary, and I believe the record supports that conclusion.

## The Stated Reason for Denial

The notice states that "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I want to address this directly, and I also want to raise a concern about which policy was actually applied to my case.

## The Policy Provided Does Not Appear to Match My Procedure

The clinical guideline document I have been given for this review is titled, in its own header, "Knee Replacement/Arthroplasty." For example, it states:

> "Partial Knee Replacement Indications CMM.JT.IN.311 v2.0.2025 Partial Knee Replacement - Unicompartmental (Medial, Lateral, or Patellofemoral) Partial knee replacement (medial, lateral, or patellofemoral) is considered medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria have been met:"

My procedure is a total **hip** replacement, not a knee replacement. I have not been shown hip-specific medical necessity criteria, so I am not in a position to know whether the imaging and clinical findings in my chart were measured against the correct policy. I ask that the plan confirm, in writing, which specific policy and criteria were used to evaluate my hip replacement request, and provide me a copy of that policy.

## The Clinical Record

Regardless of which specific hip criteria apply, the record before the plan includes the following, well-documented findings:

- **Symptom duration:** 24 months of progressive hip pain, unrelieved by rest.
- **Imaging (2026-06-09):** A weight-bearing AP pelvis radiograph showing joint space narrowed to 1 mm superolaterally, with subchondral sclerosis and osteophytes.
- **Conservative treatment already completed:**
  - Supervised physical therapy focused on hip abductor strengthening and gait, 16 weeks (2026-02-22 to 2026-06-14), 16 visits completed, documented in the physical therapy discharge note.

evidence.submission_route: Use the appeal address printed on your denial letter, or call the number on the back of your insurance card and ask where member appeals are filed.
evidence.criteria_request: Joint and spine surgery go through eviCore, whose guidelines are public. Security Health also has its own 'Total Hip Replacement Surgery' policy on their PolicyTech site. Note their 'Back Surgical Procedures' and hip impingement policies now redirect to a Sanford Health login - request those in writing.
